title: Molecular line emission in NGC 4945, imaged with ALMA
question: Investigate the structure, dynamics, and composition of the dense nuclear molecular gas in NGC 4945, including its morphology (core, rotating disk, bar, spiral arms), kinematics, and the 14N/15N isotope ratio.

data.sensitivity: 0.6 mJy/beam in ≈25 km/s (HCN/HC15N windows); 0.7 mJy/beam in ≈30 km/s (CS window); ≈0.13 mJy/beam in 310 MHz continuum

what.value: Single-dish SEST peak and integrated flux densities as well as overlayed HCN and CS spectra

evidence.quote: Approximate flux densities for the blue- and redshifted line peaks, obtained from the 15-m Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope (SEST; Wang et al. 2004) and ALMA.
Overlayed spectra (red) with lower velocity resolution and larger beam size (≈1 [′] ), matched to the amplitude of our spectra, are taken from Wang et al. (2004).

what.value: VLBA position and binding mass of the circumnuclear 22 GHz H2O maser disk

evidence.loc: 3.1. Continuum emission and the position of the H 2 O maser disk
evidence.quote: Using the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) Greenhill et al. (1997) determined the position of the circumnuclear 22 GHz H 2 O maser disk, obtaining α B1950 = 13 [h] 02 [m] 32 . [s] 28 and δ B1950 = –49 [◦] 12 [′] 01 . [′′] 9

what.value: ATCA 3 mm HNC and HCO+ J=1->0 line parameters

evidence.quote: For comparison, we have also included parameters from the HNC and HCO [+] data of Cunningham & Whiteoak (2005)

what.value: Integrated line intensity ratios for NGC 253 and seven other galaxies from a 3 mm line survey

evidence.quote: For NGC 253, see Table A.2 of Aladro et al. (2015).
A comparison with the eight galaxies covered by the λ ≈ 3 mm line survey of Aladro et al. (2015) provides additional insights.

what.value: Molecular Einstein-A coefficients and collision rates for critical density calculations

evidence.loc: 4.2. Why are some lines absorbed and others not?
evidence.quote: Using the Leiden Atomic and Molecular database (LAMBDA; Sch¨oier et al. 2005; van der Tak et al. 2007) and for CH 3 C 2 H Askne et al. (1984), we can obtain critical densities

external_data.citation: LAMBDA (Schöier et al. 2005; van der Tak et al. 2007); Askne et al. (1984)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image 3 mm continuum and spectral line cubes
recipe.method: Calibrate visibility data, subtract continuum using linear fits to line-free frequency intervals, and image both continuum-included and continuum-subtracted cubes with Briggs robust 0.0 and +2.0

recipe.goal: Measure continuum and velocity-integrated molecular source sizes, positions, flux densities, and disk inclinations
recipe.method: Create primary-beam corrected moment 0 maps and fit 2D Gaussians using the CASA viewer; derive inclination from minor-to-major axis ratio
assumptions: Flat disk with azimuthal symmetry for inclination derivation

recipe.goal: Extract regional spectra, measure line intensity ratios, and determine the 14N/15N isotope ratio
recipe.method: Extract spectra over 30'' x 30'' and sub-regions as well as single 1'' pixels at the unabsorbed line wings (V = 430 and 710 km s^-1); compute line ratios and derive 14N/15N from H13CN/HC15N
key_parameters: Pixel size 1'' x 1''; velocities V = 430 km s^-1 and 710 km s^-1; 7-channel smoothing (≈23 km s^-1) for HC15N window

recipe.goal: Analyze velocity fields, velocity dispersions, PV diagrams, and enclosed dynamical mass
recipe.method: Compute moment 1, moment 2, and major-axis PV diagrams from robust +2.0 cubes clipped at 5 sigma; derive enclosed mass from CH3C2H rotation velocity at r = 2.45''
key_parameters: Briggs robust = +2.0; 5 sigma clipping for moment 1 and 2 maps
assumptions: Spherical/disk mass distribution parameter eta = 1 in equation (1) of Mauersberger et al. (1996); D = 3.8 Mpc

recipe.goal: Model 3D nuclear disk kinematics and radial outflow with tilted rings
recipe.method: Simultaneously fit four spectral lines (c-C3H2 2_12-1_01, CH3C2H 5_0-4_0, c-C3H2 4_32-4_23, H42alpha) in the naturally weighted data cube using 3D tilted-ring modeling in TiRiFiC
key_parameters: Reference frequency 85.45727 GHz; V_exp = V_RAD + |z| * DVRA with V_RAD = 0; shared V_rot, i, PA, and center across 4 lines; independent surface brightness, scale height, and dispersion
assumptions: All four lines share rotation velocity, inclination, position angle, and central position; radial velocity varies linearly with vertical height |z| parallel to the main disk

recipe.goal: Image near-systemic velocity emission to identify the bar and spiral-like arms
recipe.method: Integrate primary-beam corrected HCN J=1->0 and CS J=2->1 emission (robust 0.0) over the velocity interval 585 - 612 km s^-1 where nuclear absorption is weak
key_parameters: Velocity interval 585 - 612 km s^-1; Briggs robust = 0.0
assumptions: Inclination i ≈ 75 deg for deprojecting bar and arm sizes

answer_key.quantity: Nitrogen isotope ratio 14N/15N

evidence.quote: A nitrogen isotope ratio of [14] N/ [15] N ≈ 200–450 is estimated.

To summarize, the measured range of ratios, [14] N/ [15] N ≈ 200 – 500, which we find in NGC 4945, is not in contradiction with the traditional view of [15] N being mainly synthesized in low mass stars.

answer_key.quantity: Enclosed dynamical mass inside r = 2.45'' (≈45 pc)

evidence.quote: The velocity field of the nuclear disk, derived from CH 3 C 2 H, provides evidence for rigid rotation in the inner few arcseconds and a dynamical mass of M tot = (2.1±0.2) × 10 [8] M ⊙ inside a galactocentric radius of 2 . [′′] 45 (≈45 pc)

At a radius of 2 . [′′] 45 (≈45 pc) and with a rotation velocity of 140 km s [−][1] we obtain with equation (1) of Mauersberger et al. (1996; η = 1) an enclosed mass of M 2.45 = 2.1 × 10 [8] M ⊙ with an estimated error of 10%

evidence.quote: Modeling this nuclear disk located farther inside (r [<] ∼100 pc) with tilted rings provides a good fit by inferring a coplanar outflow reaching a characteristic deprojectd velocity of ≈50 km s [−][1] .
